_note: Cards for the Data Structures and Algorithm Patterns sections. 'pattern' must match a name in patterns.json (it links problems and videos); 'group' picks the section; 'title' is the card heading (defaults to the pattern).

spot: Need to look something up fast (seen before? how many?)
techniques.idea: Trade memory for time: a HashMap/HashSet turns repeated O(n) scans into O(1) lookups. Prefix sums answer range-sum questions in O(1).
techniques.title: Arrays & Hash Maps

techniques.idea: Use a dummy head to avoid edge cases, fast/slow pointers for middle and cycles, and re-link pointers carefully (save next first).
techniques.title: Linked Lists

spot: Most recent unfinished item (function calls, nested strings)
techniques.idea: A stack remembers what's still open. A monotonic stack keeps elements in sorted order and pops the ones a new element 'beats'.
techniques.complexity: O(n): each element pushed and popped once
techniques.title: Stacks & Queues

spot: Repeatedly take the best next option (scheduling, Dijkstra)
techniques.idea: A PriorityQueue gives the min (or max) in O(1) and updates in O(log n). For 'top k', keep a heap of size k.
techniques.title: Heaps & Priority Queues

spot: Anything on a binary tree / BST
techniques.idea: Most tree problems are one recursive function: solve left, solve right, combine. Use BFS with a queue when the problem is about levels.
techniques.title: Trees & BSTs

spot: Autocomplete, word search in a grid
techniques.idea: A tree of characters: each path from the root spells a prefix. Lookups cost O(word length), independent of how many words are stored.
techniques.title: Tries

techniques.idea: Model cells or items as nodes, then BFS/DFS with a visited set. Topological sort for ordering, Dijkstra with a heap for weighted shortest paths.
techniques.complexity: O(V + E); Dijkstra O(E log V)
techniques.title: Graphs

techniques.idea: Work layer by layer, or with index formulas. Rotate 90° clockwise = transpose + reverse each row.
techniques.title: Matrices (2-D grids)

spot: Sorted array, or you can sort it
techniques.idea: Move two indices toward each other (or one fast, one slow). Each step discards options you can prove won't help, so the whole scan is O(n).
techniques.complexity: O(n) after an O(n log n) sort if needed

spot: Longest / shortest / count with a condition
techniques.idea: Grow the window on the right; when it breaks the rule, shrink from the left until it's valid again. Every element enters and leaves once.

spot: "Minimum x such that…" / "maximum x such that…"
Answer space is monotonic (Koko speed, capacity, days)
techniques.idea: Keep an invariant on [lo, hi) and halve it. Works on indices AND on the answer itself when a feasibility check is monotonic.
techniques.complexity: O(log n), or O(n log range) on the answer

techniques.idea: Sort by start, then sweep: merge when the next start ≤ current end. For 'how many at once', sort starts and ends separately or use a min-heap of end times.

spot: Build a solution step by step with choices
techniques.idea: It's DFS on a tree of choices that you build as you go. Choose → recurse → un-choose (path.remove). Two questions: what are the choices at each step, and when is a path complete?

spot: Count ways / min cost / max value
Choices at each step and overlapping subproblems
techniques.idea: Define dp[state] = answer for a smaller problem, write the recurrence from earlier states, fill in order (or memoize the recursion).

spot: A locally best choice provably leads to the global best
techniques.idea: Make the best choice now and never revisit it. Always sanity-check with a counterexample or an exchange argument before trusting it.
techniques.complexity: Usually O(n) or O(n log n) with sorting

spot: Character counts, expansion around a center
techniques.idea: Use StringBuilder for building, char arrays or int[26] for counts, and 'expand around center' for palindromes.
Look for a formula or invariant. Use long to avoid overflow, gcd to normalize ratios, n & (n − 1) to drop the lowest set bit.

spot: Each operation must be O(1) / O(log n)
techniques.idea: Combine structures so each one covers what the others can't: HashMap + doubly linked list (LRU), list + index map (random O(1)), TreeMap for ordered access.
Guard shared state with a lock; wait on conditions in a while loop; signal the other side after changing state. Semaphores work for counting resources.
